exercises.questionText: Calculate the area of the shape, correct to 2 decimal places. The shape is a trapezium with parallel sides $7.3\text{ mm}$ (top) and $15.2\text{ mm}$ (bottom) and a perpendicular height of $6.1\text{ mm}$.

steps: Given: parallel sides $a = 7.3\text{ mm}$, $b = 15.2\text{ mm}$, height $h = 6.1\text{ mm}$. Goal: the area $A$.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the area of the trapezium is $68.63\text{ mm}^2$ (correct to 2 decimal places).
solution.tip: Add the two parallel sides first, then halve, then multiply by the perpendicular height.

exercises.questionText: Calculate the area of the ellipse, correct to 1 decimal place. The ellipse has semi-major axis $8\text{ cm}$ and semi-minor axis $5\text{ cm}$.

solution.formula: Area of an ellipse: $A = \pi ab$, where $a$ and $b$ are the semi-major and semi-minor axes
steps: Given: $a = 8\text{ cm}$, $b = 5\text{ cm}$. Goal: the area $A$.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the area of the ellipse is $125.7\text{ cm}^2$ (correct to 1 decimal place).
solution.tip: Use the half-lengths (semi-axes), not the full widths of the ellipse.

exercises.questionText:
MC Select the total surface area of the rectangular prism from the following. The prism has length $3.2\text{ m}$, width $2\text{ m}$ and height $1.5\text{ m}$.
A. $9.6\text{ m}^2$  B. $14.2\text{ m}^2$  C. $22.0\text{ m}^2$  D. $28.4\text{ m}^2$

solution.formula: TSA of a rectangular prism: $\text{TSA} = 2(lw + lh + wh)$
steps: Given: $l = 3.2\text{ m}$, $w = 2\text{ m}$, $h = 1.5\text{ m}$. Goal: the total surface area.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the total surface area is $28.4\text{ m}^2$; the answer is D.
solution.tip: Option B (14.2) is only half the answer: each face appears twice, so remember to multiply by 2.

exercises.questionText: Calculate the total surface area of the sphere, correct to 1 decimal place. The sphere has a diameter of $15\text{ cm}$.

steps: Given: diameter $= 15\text{ cm}$, so $r = \frac{15}{2} = 7.5\text{ cm}$. Goal: the total surface area.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the total surface area of the sphere is $706.9\text{ cm}^2$ (correct to 1 decimal place).
solution.tip: The 15 cm line passes through the centre, so it is the diameter; halve it to get the radius.

exercises.questionText: Calculate the volume of the solid. The solid is a cone with base area $A = 3\text{ cm}^2$ and perpendicular height $4\text{ cm}$.

steps: Given: base area $A = 3\text{ cm}^2$, height $H = 4\text{ cm}$. Goal: the volume $V$.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the volume of the cone is $4\text{ cm}^3$.
solution.tip: A cone holds one-third of the volume of a cylinder with the same base and height, so don't forget the $\frac{1}{3}$.

exercises.questionText: Calculate the area of the shape, correct to 1 decimal place. The shape is part of a ring (annulus): a large circle of radius $2 + 3 = 5\text{ cm}$ with a small circle of radius $2\text{ cm}$ removed from its centre (the ring is $3\text{ cm}$ wide), and a $45^\circ$ sector cut out of the ring.

solution.formula: Area of a sector: $A = \frac{\theta}{360^\circ} \times \pi r^2$; shaded area = outer sector $-$ inner sector
steps: Given: inner radius $r = 2\text{ cm}$, outer radius $R = 2 + 3 = 5\text{ cm}$, missing angle $45^\circ$. Goal: the area of the shape.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the area of the shape is $57.7\text{ cm}^2$ (correct to 1 decimal place).
solution.tip: The outer radius is measured from the centre: $2 + 3 = 5$ cm, not 3 cm.

exercises.questionText:
A council park is shown below. The park is an L-shape: the top side is $240\text{ m}$ and the left side is $100\text{ m}$. Along the bottom, a $80\text{ m}$ horizontal edge runs from the bottom-left corner, then the boundary steps down $30\text{ m}$, and continues to the right side, so the right-hand part of the park extends $30\text{ m}$ further down than the left. All corners are right angles.
A worker charges $\$30$ per $1000\text{ m}^2$ to mow the grass. Determine how much it will cost the council to have the grass mown.

solution.formula: Composite area = sum of rectangles; cost = (area $\div 1000$) $\times$ rate
steps: Given: top rectangle $240\text{ m} \times 100\text{ m}$; lower rectangle of width $240 - 80 = 160\text{ m}$ and height $30\text{ m}$; rate $\$30$ per $1000\text{ m}^2$. Goal: the cost of mowing.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore it will cost the council $\$864$ to have the grass mown.
solution.tip: Split an L-shape into two rectangles and find any missing side by subtracting known lengths.

exercises.questionText:
MC Select the total surface area of the object shown from the following. The object is a cone with a hemisphere on top. The radius of the hemisphere and of the cone is $2.5\text{ cm}$, and the perpendicular height of the cone is $9\text{ cm}$.
A. $109.96\text{ cm}^2$  B. $112.63\text{ cm}^2$  C. $151.9\text{ cm}^2$  D. $124.36\text{ cm}^2$

solution.formula: Curved surface of a hemisphere $= 2\pi r^2$; curved surface of a cone $= \pi rl$ with $l = \sqrt{r^2 + h^2}$ (Pythagoras)
steps: Given: $r = 2.5\text{ cm}$, cone height $h = 9\text{ cm}$. Goal: the total outside surface area.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the total surface area is $112.63\text{ cm}^2$; the answer is B.
solution.tip: The 9 cm is the vertical height, not the slant height; option A comes from wrongly using 9 cm as the slant height.

exercises.questionText: Determine the volume of the triangular prism. The cross-section is a right-angled triangle with one shorter side $3\text{ mm}$ and hypotenuse $5\text{ mm}$; the length of the prism is $10\text{ mm}$.

solution.formula: Volume of a prism: $V = AH$, with triangle area $A = \frac{1}{2}bh$; Pythagoras' theorem $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$
steps: Given: right-angled triangle with side $3\text{ mm}$ and hypotenuse $5\text{ mm}$; prism length $H = 10\text{ mm}$. Goal: the volume.
Find the missing side $h$ of the triangle: $h^2 = 5^2 - 3^2 = 25 - 9 = 16$
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the volume of the triangular prism is $60\text{ mm}^3$.
solution.tip: The triangle's area needs the two perpendicular sides, so use Pythagoras to find the missing one first.

exercises.questionText:
MC Select the volume of the object from the following. The object is a cylinder of diameter $10\text{ cm}$ and height $20\text{ cm}$ with a cone of the same diameter and height $15\text{ cm}$ on top.
A. $2748.9\text{ cm}^3$  B. $1701.7\text{ cm}^3$  C. $1963.5\text{ cm}^3$  D. $7854\text{ cm}^3$

steps: Given: $r = \frac{10}{2} = 5\text{ cm}$, cylinder height $20\text{ cm}$, cone height $15\text{ cm}$. Goal: the total volume.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the volume is $1963.5\text{ cm}^3$; the answer is C.
solution.tip: Halve the 10 cm diameter to get the radius before squaring.

exercises.questionText:
MC The volume of the frustum of a square-based pyramid, with top square side $y$, bottom square side $x$ and height $h$, is given by:
A. $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi(x^2 + y^2)$  B. $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi(x^2 + xy + y^2)$  C. $V = \frac{1}{3}h\pi(x^2 + xy + y^2)$  D. $V = \frac{1}{3}h(x^2 + xy + y^2)$

solution.formula: Volume of a frustum: $V = \frac{1}{3}h(A_1 + \sqrt{A_1A_2} + A_2)$, where $A_1$, $A_2$ are the areas of the two parallel faces
steps: Given: square faces of side $x$ and $y$, height $h$. Goal: choose the volume formula.
Check: a volume must contain the height, and the faces are squares (no $\pi$), so only D is possible.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore $V = \frac{1}{3}h(x^2 + xy + y^2)$; the answer is D.
solution.tip: $\pi$ only appears when there are circles; a square-based solid has no $\pi$ in its volume.

exercises.questionText: The volume of a ball is given by the formula $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3$. Evaluate the radius of a ball with a volume of $384.66\text{ cm}^3$. Give your answer correct to 1 decimal place.

solution.formula: Volume of a sphere: $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3$, rearranged to $r = \sqrt[3]{\frac{3V}{4\pi}}$
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the radius of the ball is $4.5\text{ cm}$ (correct to 1 decimal place).
solution.tip: Undo the operations in reverse order and finish with a cube root, not a square root.

exercises.questionText:
MC Determine what effect doubling the radius and halving the height of a cone will have on its volume.
A. The volume will be the same.
B. The volume will be halved.
C. The volume will be doubled.
D. The volume will be quadrupled.

solution.formula: Volume of a cone: $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h$
steps: Given: original cone $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h$; new radius $2r$, new height $\frac{h}{2}$. Goal: compare the volumes.
$V_{\text{new}} = 2V$, so the volume is doubled (option C).
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the volume will be doubled; the answer is C.
solution.tip: The radius is squared, so doubling it multiplies the volume by 4, not 2.

exercises.questionText: Using Heron's formula, evaluate the area of the triangle, correct to 1 decimal place. The triangle has sides $9\text{ cm}$, $4\text{ cm}$ and $7\text{ cm}$.

solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the area of the triangle is $13.4\text{ cm}^2$ (correct to 1 decimal place).
solution.tip: $s$ is the semi-perimeter: half of the perimeter, not the full perimeter.

exercises.questionText: A cylindrical soft drink can has a diameter of $6.4\text{ cm}$ and a height of $14.3\text{ cm}$. If the can is only half full, determine what capacity of soft drink remains, to the nearest millilitre.

solution.formula: Volume of a cylinder: $V = \pi r^2 h$; $1\text{ cm}^3 = 1\text{ mL}$
steps: Given: $r = \frac{6.4}{2} = 3.2\text{ cm}$, $h = 14.3\text{ cm}$, the can is half full. Goal: the volume of drink in mL.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore about $230\text{ mL}$ of soft drink remains (to the nearest millilitre).
solution.tip: Remember to halve the full volume, and that $1\text{ cm}^3$ holds exactly $1\text{ mL}$.
